rationale: Attempt-00 passed SMT, compiled, and passed numerical checks with block_M=32,block_N=64,block_K=32,num_stages=3, reaching simulated_us=147.72 (a simulator estimate, not hardware measurement; Metal ran the exact source/config/TIR, CUDA binary was not executed). Since M=32, only block_M=32 divides M so 64/128 are infeasible; domain narrowed to [32] to avoid wasted variables while keeping all other domains nonempty. Traffic is dominated by 1/block_N term (M is tiny), so increasing block_N to 128 should cut traffic substantially; pipeline cost favors larger block_K and more stages to reduce per-iteration overhead. We reweight traffic and pipeline to 2 to prioritize latency-driving terms, reduce launches and footprint to 0.5 since N/block_N launches (~32-64 total) and epilogue smem (~16KB) are already small. Shared budget kept at 32768 with hard portability cap 32768; with block_M=32 the max term max(2*block_K*(32+128)*3, 4*32*128)=max(30720,16384)=30720 fits. Next hypothesis: try block_N=128 with larger block_K and num_stages to reduce traffic/pipeline; if simulator improves, keep; also verify actual compiled smem does not exceed the portability cap for stage-3 block_K=64 cases.
